architecture_brief:
Hermes upstream main was 663362680b on 2026-09-30 and had reached 298a01c79b by the end of the sweep (about 700 commits/day). Hermes is a narrow-waist core with a wide plugin edge.

Turn pipeline. AIAgent.run_conversation takes a turn lease, then runs build_turn_context. Memory prefetch and pre_llm_call context are attached to the CURRENT user message's api_content sidecar, so replay stays byte-identical. The phase loop then runs, with every phase dispatched through conversation_loop._run_phase:
- assemble request
- preflight gate
- API retry loop (llm_request/llm_execution middleware; transform_api_error_classification)
- then either a tool round (8 workers or fewer, segmented batches, tool_request/tool_execution middleware, pre/post_tool_call) or finish_text_response
- then stop gates: verify-on-stop (opt-in since #84383), pre_verify (only after edits), and the kanban guard.
finalize_turn then does persist, post_llm_call, ContextEngine.on_turn_complete, memory sync_all + queue_prefetch, and the background-review fork. It also fires plugin on_session_end, which runs every turn despite its name.

Hard invariants:
1. The per-conversation prompt cache is sacred. The system prompt stays byte-stable across its stable/context/volatile tiers. Compression is the only sanctioned cache break. Mid-conversation content must ride a user message or a tool result. Per-turn switching of the main model breaks the cache.
2. Roles strictly alternate. The only synthetic user rows are /steer and the flagged stop-gate nudges.
3. Profile scope is bound per activity. Use spawn_context_thread, secret_scope and hermes_home_key; background threads must carry their ContextVars.
4. Code shape: split files over ~2k lines; no elif ladders on names, no re-export shims, no defensive try/except-pass.

Footprint ladder, in order of preference: extend existing → CLI+skill → check_fn tool → plugin → catalog MCP → core tool. The surface already includes:
- 41 VALID_HOOKS. Examples: pre/post_api_request, whose payload already carries first_chunk_at and context_length; transform_tool_result (str-only); transform_terminal_output; pre_verify; subagent_*; on_skill_lifecycle; approval and kanban observers.
- 4 middleware kinds.
- 37 PluginContext members, including a single-slot register_context_engine, register_auxiliary_task, ctx.llm.complete_structured, and register_system_prompt_section (after_memory, ≤4k).
- ABCs: MemoryProvider (builtin plus ONE external; the provider owns prefetch caching), ContextEngine (select_context is request-only and fails open), ProviderProfile, SecretSource.
- Hook timeout is 30 s. pre_tool_call fails closed.

Policy:
- The in-tree memory-provider set is closed.
- No third-party-product plugins in plugins/. They ship as a standalone repo plus a SHA-pinned plugin-catalog/*.yaml (350 entries today; Jev, z0, Bend, SoL-Pi and Kerdoios belong there).
- New hooks only with a real fire site and a consumer. The hook taxonomy (#64231) is still open.
- When 3+ PRs compete for the same category, design the ABC first.
- Use config.yaml, not new HERMES_* env vars. No outbound telemetry without opt-in.
- Each fix needs 1–2 invariant tests that are red on base. Scope or config changes need E2E against a temp HERMES_HOME, including A→B→A multiplex. No change-detector tests. Run tests only through scripts/run_tests.sh.
- Salvage by cherry-pick, preserving authorship.
- Maintainers want ~3 open PRs per contributor. kvnloo has 13 open, 1 merged and 175 closed.

Evidence culture: evals/ holds two-arm A/B harnesses whose verdicts live in SUMMARY/SCORECARD files: core_tool_deferral (288 runs), toolperf_abeval, the compaction recall exam (±3.3 pt noise), readtool, codebase_navigability, and token_accounting replay_gates. Caching-adjacent changes need a cache-read ratio measured before and after. Teknium rejected prune-first compaction because of cache breaks, and named summary identifier retention as the real gap.

What this means for the experiment factory:
- Fork CI is unusable for this. Fork PR CI shows action_required or stays queued, and ACT-001 disabled 253 workflows. Run experiments locally or on k8s instead: FakeLLMServer or scripted replay at $0, or local llama.cpp on a single RTX 3080 Ti, where latency cells must run serially.
- 97 of the 138 focus fork branches are more than 5k commits behind main. So a staging branch must be a promote/<slug>-vN rebuild recipe: one commit on fresh main, plus a manifest of member-branch SHAs, the RFC/issue, and the eval receipts. Never use one as a merge target for stale branches.
- Third-party consumers promote as catalog entries, not core PRs.

features.title: Capability-gated computer-use capture-mode projection
features.one_liner: Pass the ax/vision capture mode to cua-driver output selectors when the driver advertises them, so it stops producing a screenshot or AX tree that Hermes then discards; som mode and older drivers are unchanged.
features.evidence_summary: Xipong ran it on Windows against a Unity window with cua-driver 0.28.2 in vision mode: main timed out at 3.942 s, the PR returned a valid 321x608 PNG in 2.029 s (#113389). The vision path still discards the tree on main, and the file blob d60bce2b is identical at the branch base and on main. That a clean rebase works is unverified. The maintainer-salvaged AX-walk bound (#116512→#118964) is a precedent for this class of change. On bare Xvfb the effect is null (26–32 ms), so the next measurement should use the sandbox-desktop image.

features.one_liner: Keep test suites from writing chatter into users' external memory. Retrieval stays live while turn sync, mirrors, the session-end flush and tool writes are suppressed. A prerequisite for live factory arms.

features.title: Lean per-session prefix and task-conditioned skill exposure
features.one_liner: Cut the static prefix that every cold session must write. Hide a skill only if the selector misses a needed skill no more than once in 30.

Hiding 45 skills saved about 5.7k tokens, but selectors missed needed skills 2–3 times in 30, so it was NOT promoted. Hermes's #95681 already cut about 15–20K tokens per call, so headroom is smaller.

features.title: Bounded-candidate ranking for session_search FTS
features.one_liner: Rank an inner LIMIT-N candidate set instead of applying ORDER BY rank or timestamp to every match.

SoL-Pi EPR is one of the 4 mechanisms behind its 44.7–49% token cut, but it was never isolated, and the TB4 solve rate fell 18→15 of 63. Hermes does only 40/60 head/tail truncation. The toolperf err_big_output trap can serve as the information-loss guard.
